results.title: Brain region identification
results.question: What are the major subdivisions of the Drosophila mushroom body?
results.response: The major subdivisions of the Drosophila [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are the calyx, pedunculus, and mushroom body lobe system, as recorded in VFB. VFB describes the mushroom body as divided into: the calyx, which is closest to the cortex and receives sensory interneuron afferents; the pedunculus, which is a thick axon bundle extending from the calyx to the base of the lobes; and the mushroom body lobe system, which consists of a vertical branch and a medial branch, which have different structures at different life stages. VFB holds various data related to the mushroom body, including images, neurons with some part in the mushroom body, parts of the mushroom body, and tracts/nerves innervating the mushroom body. To explore the structure and components of the mushroom body further, you can use VFB to list all available images of mushroom body, or to find neurons with synaptic terminals in mushroom body, among other queries.

results.question: What types of Kenyon cells exist in the adult Drosophila brain?

This information comes from the VFB database. VFB holds [37](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of Kenyon cell") records of subclasses of Kenyon cell, which may provide further details on the types of Kenyon cells. results.question: What are the main components of the Drosophila central complex and what functions are they associated with?
results.response:
The Drosophila central complex is a structure in the insect brain that plays a crucial role in navigation, locomotion, and spatial memory. According to general knowledge in the field of Drosophila neuroscience, the main components of the central complex include the ellipsoid body, the fan-shaped body, the noduli, and the protocerebral bridge. 

VFB does not currently hold specific data on the functions associated with each of these components. However, the connectome data indicates that the central complex is involved in the integration of sensory information and the regulation of motor outputs. 

For more information on the central complex and its components, further queries can be made to VFB to explore available data on neuronal projections, connectivity, and gene expression.

results.title: Neuron characterisation
results.question: What is known about the LPLC2 visual neuron type? Where is it, what does it connect to, and what is its function?
results.response:
The LPLC2 visual neuron type has specific characteristics and functions. According to VFB, it is a type of Lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron whose cell body lies in the dorsal area of the lateral cell body rind, as described by Wu et al., 2016. The LPLC2 neuron has a distinct dendritic arbor in each lobula plate layer, extending outwards from the main fiber in the direction of motion detection for the layer, as reported by Klapoetke et al., 2017. This arrangement allows it to detect looming (expansion) stimuli. 

In the lobula, the LPLC2 neuron has its main dendritic arbors in layers 4 and 5B, with minor processes in layer 5A, and presynaptic sites in layer 4, as described by Wu et al., 2016, and Tanaka and Clark, 2022. Its arbors span approximately 25 lobula optic columns, overlapping with other LPLC2 cells, according to Wu et al., 2016. The LPLC2 neuron projects to an optic glomerulus of the PVLP, anterior to LPLC1 and dorsal to LC4, as reported by Wu et al., 2016. 

The activity of the LPLC2 neuron elicits a jump escape response, as described by Wu et al., 2016, and Klapoetke et al., 2017. VFB records show that there are approximately 80 of these cells per optic lobe, as reported by Wu et al., 2016, and they are cholinergic, according to Davis et al., 2020. 

VFB does not currently hold comprehensive data on the full range of connections of the LPLC2 neuron type beyond what is described above.

results.title: Complete neuron profile
results.question: Give me a comprehensive profile of the giant fiber neuron: its anatomy, connectivity, available driver lines, and relevant publications.
results.response:
The [giant fiber neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004020 "Open giant fiber neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") is a large adult descending neuron that controls jump escape behavior, with a large cell body located posterior to the lower protocerebrum and a large descending axon. It can be identified by its large descending axon, which is several times larger than any other axon in the cervical connective. The giant fiber neuron enters the cervical connective via the posterior cerebro-cervical fascicle and descends on the ipsilateral side, in the dorsal cervical fasciculus. In the brain, it has dendritic arborization in the ipsilateral zones A and B of the antennal mechanosensory and motor center, where it receives substantial input from zone A and B Johnston organ neurons. It also arborizes in the posterior ventrolateral protocerebrum and gorget. The giant fiber neuron enters the ventral nerve cord near the dorsal midline and extends posteroventrally to the mesothoracic neuromere, where it turns ventrolaterally, and ends abruptly without branching.

VFB holds information on the giant fiber neuron, including [23](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of DNp01") images of DNp01, [5](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,SplitsTargeting "Run in VFB: Splits targeting DNp01") splits targeting DNp01, and [14](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in DNp01") records of transgene expression in DNp01. The downstream connectivity classes for DNp01 are also available, with [389](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for DNp01") records, and the upstream connectivity classes for DNp01, with [472](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for DNp01") records.

Relevant publications for the giant fiber neuron include Thomas and Wyman, 1984; Power, 1948; Koto et al., 1981; Namiki et al., 2018; Ito et al., 2014; Kamikouchi et al., 2009; Matsuo et al., 2016; and Kim et al., 2020.
